Subject: Renewal conversation — premium SLA + increased capacity needs

Hi Mina / Ben,

Hope you’re well. Our contract comes up for renewal in late May and we’ve seen a steady growth in inference volume over Q1: average TPS up ~2.2x and peak windows causing token spikes. We’re evaluating two asks for the renewal:

- Move to Redwood’s Premium SLA for tighter latency guarantees (we're targeting p99 <= 250ms for our standard 2k token prompts).
- Reserve additional burst-able capacity (estimate: 4x current reserved gpus during business hours + a warm standby for weekend spikes).

We need a concise proposal that includes: pricing for a 12-month vs 36-month term, how burst reservations behave (warm standby vs cold cold-start), overage pricing, and any support escalation/response commitments tied to premium. Also, procurement will need a sample SOW and a clear MOP for billing overage events.

Can you share an initial sketch this week? We have procurement / finance calls the week of 4/19.

Thanks,
Sanjay

--
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform
NeuroCart Inc.

Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — premium SLA + increased capacity needs

Sanjay — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can support that set of requirements and we have two routes that align with what you described. I attached a draft SOW and our pricing bands for reserved + burst capacity. See highlights below.

Option A — Premium Reserved + Elastic Burst (12-month / 36-month pricing)
- Dedicated reserved pool sized to baseline throughput (we recommend reserving capacity for 2.5x current baseline; we show line items for 2.5x and 4x in the sheet)
- Elastic Burst window: warm standby nodes that maintain warmed KV caches (minutes-scale spin up) for predictable business-hour surges; cold pool for unexpected spikes (longer spin up, lower cost)
- SLA: p99 latency guardrail 250ms for requests routed to reserved pool; best-effort for cold pool with fallback to slightly larger model variant to maintain throughput.
- Support: Premium SLA includes 1-hour P0 response and prioritized runbook escalation; add-on: 24/7 on-call rotation (+ cost).

Option B — Committed Throughput + Credits (more cost-optimized for long tails)
- Commit to throughput (tokens/sec) with smaller reserved GPU count and higher burst capacity credits allocated monthly.
- Overage: explicit token-based overage pricing in the sheet; we can cap monthly overage at a negotiated % to provide billing predictability.

Attachments: NeuroCart-SOW-v2.pdf, RC-pricing-bands-2027.xlsx, support-credit-model.csv

Next steps I propose:
- Quick call (30m) early next week to align on which option matches your procurement constraints.
- If you prefer, I can produce a redline-friendly SOW and a mutual action plan tied to contract milestones.

I’ll leave pricing detail to Ben but happy to walk the technical guarantees / warm-standby behavior.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina — the summary is helpful. A few clarifying items from our end before we sync with procurement: 

1) Warm standby behavior: can you confirm the typical spin-up tail for warm standby (we prefer < 90s to reach p99 guardrail) and what cache-warm semantics you guarantee for KV cache reuse across bursts?
2) Billing model: procurement prefers a single committed line item + monthly burst credits. Can you map Option A into a committed reservation + monthly credit allocation with a recommended credit sizing heuristic?
3) Term flexibility: we’re interested in 12-month with an option to extend at a fixed uplift vs a 36-month discounted commit — procurement will want the uplift numbers for quick approval.
4) Compliance: we need confirmation about audit logs retention and whether dedicated pools can be pinned to a US-only region for data residency.

If you can include those clarifications in the pricing workbook and the SOW we’ll be in a good spot for our internal finance/ops sync on 4/19. Also — can we ask for a one-week demo of the warm-standby burst behavior scoped to our traffic pattern (I can provide a sample load profile)?

— Sanjay
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Forwarding NeuroCart thread — Sanjay asked the key clarifications (see below). Internal notes / proposed ask from pricing: 

- Proposed commercial structure to send to NeuroCart: 12-month commit with optional 12-month extension at +4% uplift; 36-month commit at -12% off list. Include a monthly burst credit pool sized at ~30% of committed tokens; work with Mina on a heuristic mapping.
- Technical guarantees: warm standby spin-up target 60s (internal SLO), KV reuse documented to support ~80% cache hit within session windows if warm nodes are used. This will be in the technical addendum.
- Compliance: confirm US-only pinning available for Dedicated pools; ops will need a ticket template for audit log delivery (we have a playbook).

Action items assigned:
- Priyom: update RC-pricing-bands-2027.xlsx with two commercial lines (12 / 36) and an explicit burst-credit table; include a capped overage example.
- Mina: draft the mutual action plan + runbook snippet describing the warm-standby demo and data residency notes.
- Ben: draft the email to procurement with the commercial summary and DS link.

I’ll prepare the commercial quote after Priyom’s update — target sending the commercial deck to NeuroCart on 4/14 afternoon.
